lines.en: Kenji, today’s exercise is a mystery. A stranger left a bag in the classroom, and we have to make an inference from each clue.
lines.pt: Kenji, o exercício de hoje é um mistério. Um desconhecido deixou uma bolsa na sala e temos de fazer uma inferência a partir de cada pista.

lines.en: Let’s see. The coffee is still hot, so the owner seems to have left only a few minutes ago.
lines.pt: Vejamos. O café ainda está quente, então o dono parece ter saído há poucos minutos.

lines.en: Good. And the laptop is open, so he appears to be working on something. What else do the clues tell us?
lines.pt: Bom. E o notebook está aberto, então ele parece estar trabalhando em algo. O que mais as pistas nos dizem?

lines.en: There’s a ticket in the bag. I’m sure that he is travelling today, because it is for a flight at six.
lines.pt: Há uma passagem na bolsa. Tenho certeza de que ele viaja hoje, porque é para um voo às seis.

lines.en: Careful. The fact that he has a ticket doesn’t prove that he is leaving. He may have bought it for someone else.
lines.pt: Cuidado. O fato de ele ter uma passagem não prova que vai viajar. Ele pode ter comprado para outra pessoa.

lines.en: True. Still, the idea that he forgot the bag on purpose seems unlikely, since there is a passport inside it.
lines.pt: Verdade. Mesmo assim, a ideia de que ele esqueceu a bolsa de propósito parece improvável, já que há um passaporte dentro.

lines.en: Excellent reasoning. Now imagine the owner returns. He would be sorry to have caused trouble and glad to have found the bag, wouldn’t he?
lines.pt: Ótimo raciocínio. Agora imagine que o dono volta. Ele ficaria triste por ter causado problema e feliz por ter encontrado a bolsa, não é?

lines.en: Yes, and he would probably be surprised to have been given so much attention by the whole class.
lines.pt: Sim, e provavelmente ficaria surpreso por ter recebido tanta atenção da turma inteira.

lines.en: Exactly. I’m pleased that you used the perfect and continuous forms correctly.
lines.pt: Exatamente. Fico satisfeita que você usou corretamente as formas perfeita e contínua.

lines.en: Thanks. I’m afraid that I still mix up seems to be and seems to have, but I am getting better.
lines.pt: Obrigada. Receio ainda confundir seems to be e seems to have, mas estou melhorando.

lines.en: Don’t worry. It’s nice to be working with students who ask questions, so let’s try another mystery tomorrow morning.
lines.pt: Não se preocupe. É bom estar trabalhando com alunos que fazem perguntas, então vamos tentar outro mistério amanhã de manhã.

facts.label: Inferências
facts.sub: Revise: seems to have + participle, appears to be + -ing, sorry to have + participle, to have been + participle e the fact / I’m sure that…

facts.label: Passado
facts.sub: Para inferir o passado use seems / appears to have + particípio: The owner seems to have left. Ele já saiu, e você deduz isso pelas pistas. O café quente é a evidência.

facts.label: Presente
facts.sub: Para inferir o que acontece agora use seems / appears to be + -ing: He appears to be working. É a forma contínua. Ela mostra algo em andamento, como o notebook aberto.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Seems to have + participle looks at the past.
“The fact that” takes a full clause.
items.why: The clause has a subject and a verb.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Seems to have + participle looks at the past. → Verdadeiro (It is the perfect infinitive.)
Seems to be + -ing describes now. → Verdadeiro (It is the continuous infinitive.)
“The fact that” takes a full clause. → Verdadeiro (The clause has a subject and a verb.)

pages.title: A classroom mystery · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Thursday morning in a classroom in Atlanta. A bag sits alone on a desk. Dana adds three objects. Her student Nina looks closely. Today the class plays detective. Every clue must be explained.

“Nina, today’s exercise is a mystery. A stranger left a bag in the classroom, and we have to make an inference from each clue.” says Dana. “Let’s see. The coffee is still hot, so the owner seems to have left only a few minutes ago.” says Nina. “Good. And the laptop is open, so he appears to be working on something. What else do the clues tell us?” says Dana.
